source.author: verg
source.text: Nunc etiam interpres divom, Iove missus ab ipso testor utrumque caput celeris mandata per auras detulit; ipse deum manifesto in lumine vidi intrantem muros, vocemque his auribus hausi.
source.text_original: Nunc etiam interpres divom, Iove missus ab ipso — / testor utrumque caput — celeris mandata per auras / detulit; ipse deum manifesto in lumine vidi / intrantem muros, vocemque his auribus hausi.
source.text_english: Now, too, as messenger of the gods, sent by Jupiter himself, I call to witness both heads that he carried the commands swiftly through the air; I myself saw the god entering the walls in clear daylight, and with these ears I drank in his voice.

reuse.author: lact
reuse.text: eas igitur aures quibus est inditum nomen a uocibus hauriendis, unde uocemque his auribus hausi; aut quia uocem ipsam Graeci dsirv uocant ab auditu, per immutationem litterae aures uelut audes sunt nominatae noluit deus artifex mollibus pelliculis informare, quae pulchritudinem demerent pendulae atque flaccentes, neque duris ac solidis ossibus, ne ad usum inhabiles essent immobiles ac rigentes, sed quod esset horum medium excogitauit, ut eas cartilago mollior alligaret et haberent aptam simul ac flexibilem firmitatem.
reuse.text_original: eas igitur aures — quibus est inditum nomen a uocibus hauriendis, unde uocemque his auribus hausi; aut quia uocem ipsam Graeci d>sir)v uocant ab auditu, per immutationem litterae aures uelut audes sunt nominatae — noluit deus artifex mollibus pelliculis informare, quae pulchritudinem demerent pendulae atque flaccentes, neque duris ac solidis ossibus, ne ad usum inhabiles essent immobiles ac rigentes, sed quod esset horum medium excogitauit, ut eas cartilago mollior alligaret et haberent aptam simul ac flexibilem firmitatem.
reuse.text_english: Therefore God the craftsman did not want to shape those ears, which are given their name from the taking in of voices, from soft skins that, hanging and drooping, detract from beauty, nor from hard and solid bones, lest they be unsuitable for use through being immobile and rigid, but devised what was midway between these, so that a softer cartilage might bind them and they might have at once suitable and flexible firmness.
